newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahraini court jails 15 plot suspects - official.
newsitem.headline: Bahraini court jails 15 plot suspects - official.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Wednesday sentenced 15 people accused of involvement in an alleged pro-Iranian plot to topple the government to prison terms ranging from three to 15 years.
A government official told Reuters 15 defendants were sentenced to prison terms and 11 acquitted.
Lawyers had earlier said 16 suspects had been jailed and 10 acquitted.
The official, lawyers and sources close to the court said Ali al-Muqawi received 15 years in jail and Sheikh Jassim al-Kayat 12 years. The two were the main suspects in the plot.
They were also fined 7,000 ($18,567) and 5,000 dinars respectively.
The official said two other suspects received eight years in prison, one suspect received seven years, eight got five years and two three years. The last two were also fined 500 dinars each.

The trial of 81 suspects -- 22 of them in absentia -- began on March 1. They were accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Lawyers had said the suspects could have faced the death penalty.
They said the court would on Saturday sentence the remaining suspects.
Bahrain last June accused Iran of an attempt to topple the island's government by force. Iran denied the charge.
The verdicts were announced on the first anniversary of the execution by firing squad of Ahmed Hassan Qamber for killing a policeman.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from the largely Sunni government.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested.
